items_missed: Never asked 'How are you today?' — jumped straight into logistics
No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation — customer never knew the call structure or that it would take 10-15 minutes
Never asked how many boxes, whether there were storage stops, or whether there were additional stops
Never asked the moving-stressors question ('anything you're particularly worried about?') even though the customer volunteered a hard Thursday deadline
Did not proactively probe the garage or other extra rooms — the customer surfaced the garage totes himself
No 'pricing is super simple' opener
Never itemized what's included (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap pads, bands, tools) — only said 'the price already includes everything'
Never quoted packing service pricing or materials cost, despite the customer explicitly asking for packing help on books and lamps
Incomplete no-hidden-fees pitch — covered credit card and assembly fees, but not fuel surcharge or transportation fees
No sense-check ('does that make sense?') after the clock/minimum explanation
No estimate delivered at all — no typical time range for the job, no crew size or truck recommendation; deferred entirely to a callback after reviewing photos
No school-bus/equivalents framing and no traffic mention, even after flagging Humble-to-Houston drive time as a cost driver
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech omitted — no 'prep = shorter move = lower bill', no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip on an hourly, deadline-driven job
Never asked for the booking — created scarcity ('only tomorrow or next week') but never attempted to lock the date in
Never mentioned that no deposit is required
No confirmation-email handoff explained — no bolded-details list, no 'reply with any corrections'
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?'
No hours of operation given
No Ecobox/box-supply referral despite the customer needing to pack books and lamps
No 60c/lb baseline mentioned alongside No Worries coverage
Never acknowledged that this was a repeat customer who opened by praising the March 2025 move — a free rapport moment left on the table
top_strength: Strong, patient logistics discovery — she confirmed both addresses and zips, corrected the profile's 3-bedroom/3000 sqft assumption against what was actually moving, probed oversized and fragile items, and asked good access questions about parking-to-freight-elevator distance and elevator-to-unit walk on the 4th floor. She also stayed calm and accommodating through several minutes of the customer struggling to text photos.
coaching_note: The call ended with no estimate, no booking attempt, and no email handoff — a warm repeat customer with a hard Thursday deadline was left on 'I'll call you right back.' Even without the photos, Joanna had enough (couch, two chairs, dresser, small table, TVs, books and totes, ground-floor load, 4th-floor elevator unload, ~15ft walk) to give a typical hours range and a 2-mover recommendation, then ask for tomorrow's slot on the spot. Give a working range, ask for the booking, say 'no deposit required,' and send the confirmation email — refine the number after the photos rather than deferring the whole close.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and patient ('sure, no worries, take your time') and she used the customer's name a few times, but the warmth was transactional — she never acknowledged his opening compliment about the March 2025 move or his deadline stress beyond a flat 'I understand,' and the delivery leaned heavily on 'mm-hmm' filler and mechanical topic jumps.
audio_review_reason: The customer interrupted mid-pricing to say her voice 'got washed out,' forcing her to repeat the availability and pricing explanation — worth verifying whether this is a headset/connection issue on her line that is costing clarity on other calls.
